correctness.rationale: An arbitrary fix-S invariant binary relation on infinite equality atoms has precisely m^2 named bits, two named-generic interface subsets, and generic diagonal/off-diagonal bits. Any shortest path with repeated generic visits can be replaced by a no-longer path with a single generic intermediate (or the appropriate endpoint), because all generic-to-named and named-to-generic arcs are uniform. This gives the five exhaustive exact formulas. Named distances are the minimum of finite named-only distances and beta(c)+2+alpha(d), and off-diagonal generic distance is either one or 2+gamma; all edge and zero-length cases are included. Generic SCC dichotomy and sharp m+1 cutoff follow. Actual independently written Floyd-Warshall checker exhausts 132132 orbit encodings for m<=3 and compares 3000 m=4 samples; it does not replace the all-m proof.

value.rationale: This answers the motivated natural all-m symbolic-geodesic problem for arbitrary finitely supported directed relations on equality atoms, not an isolated finite census. Infinite pairwise distances reduce to an m-vertex directed graph and two interface sets via a closed exact min-plus rank-one correction; the procedure is cubic in support size, and it yields a generic SCC dichotomy. The explicit symbolic metric is more informative than closure decidability and may support precise reachability evaluation and distance constraints. There is no assertion of a general orbit-finite-carrier theorem.
